AR-2026F-SR15.aiSummary: This resolution would let a bill be introduced to raise Arkansas’s homestead property tax credit. The credit would reduce real property taxes on a home from $600 to $675 each year. The change would apply to assessment years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.

AR-2026F-SB8.aiSummary: Now law as Act 129, it sets the 2026-2027 budget for the Arkansas Department of Commerce and its economic development work. It funds salaries, office costs, grants, and business incentive programs, including money for community assistance, disaster recovery, the Arkansas Acceleration Fund, and super projects. The act also sets the most employees allowed in several department units for that year.

AR-2026F-SB75.aiSummary: Arkansas Act 144 changes the state revenue law and sets how state money is moved into many funds and fund accounts. It updates monthly transfer rules for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and after, including schools, health services, higher education, state agencies, counties, and cities. The act also declares an emergency, so it takes effect right away.

AR-2026F-SB20.aiSummary: Act 132 makes state money available for the Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of Medical Services, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets funds for staff pay and operating costs, Medicaid grant payments, nursing home closure costs, receivership expenses, and nursing home quality grants. It also sets rules for how Medicaid rates are calculated and lets the division change rates in some cases, with some changes needing approval from lawmakers.

AR-2026F-HB1077.aiSummary: The act sets spending and staffing limits for the Arkansas Department of Human Services, Division of County Operations, for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It includes money for salaries, operations, grants, Medicaid tobacco settlement work, emergency rental help, and Summer EBT, along with up to 2,010 regular employees and 43 extra-help workers. It also requires a yearly $7.5 million transfer from TANF funds to the Arkansas Better Chance Program and directs the department to seek a federal waiver to limit what TANF cash assistance can buy.

AR-2026F-HB1022.aiSummary: The bill would give the Arkansas Development Finance Authority money for the 2026-2027 fiscal year. It sets aside $15,000,000 for the Federal Housing Program and $2,296,487 for grants and aid tied to emergency shelters and help for homeless people and families. It also sets pay rules for agency jobs and allows up to 20 extra positions if growth needs come up. The act would take effect on July 1, 2026.
